aria: Animated recap of the Suns' 102 to 99 home win over Houston: Devin Booker's 17-footer that broke a 93-93 tie with 4:24 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 24 points, the top scorers, how the Suns won, and the next game against San Antonio.
notes: Box score from the Suns' 102–99 home win over the Houston Rockets on Nov 7, 2026, from StatMuse's full box score and quarter scores, with game details from the AP (via ABC News and Fox Sports), Field Level Media, Basketball Insiders, Roundtable and Yardbarker. All 102 Suns points and all 99 Rockets points are accounted for in the box score. The 19-point Suns lead (44–25) is from the AP, Field Level Media and Basketball Insiders; Houston's 6-point lead in the third quarter is Basketball Insiders'. Booker scored the Suns' last nine points (Field Level Media and Arizona Sports): Field Level Media's sequence is (a 17-footer, a step-back jumper, a 3-pointer and a driving layup). The Spurs' record and the Suns' standing are from the site's standings (Basketball Insiders also has Phoenix 12th in the West); the next game is from the AP and Yardbarker.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Devin Booker's 17-footer with 4:24 left that broke a 93–93 tie (Field Level Media; Roundtable has the game tied at 93 with about four and a half minutes left). It was the first of the Suns' last nine points, all scored by Booker, ending with a layup for a 102–95 lead at 2:30. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as a plain pull-up. His signature smooth mid-range stroke is shown by holding the follow-through until the ball drops: a stylized trait, not a description of this possession. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Phoenix Suns or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Booker’s listed 6-foot-5 and 206 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-8¼ wingspan at the 2015 draft combine (theScore). It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
